entry_rationale: Fade the 99.6 five-year extreme in AUDNZD at 1.2456 as a reduced-size cheap-kiwi relative-value short. Australian hike pricing and mild negative carry cap conviction, so size is half the 20 million merchant ticket and de-risk is fast if the cross extends.
entry_thesis: AUDNZD at 1.2456 is a 99.6 five-year extreme while kiwi is independently cheap versus the dollar at a 3.5 five-year percentile. Shorting the cross is the cleaner kiwi mean-reversion expression: it fades rich Aussie versus cheap kiwi without a naked long in a high-beta commodity currency while Hormuz remains the swing factor. Australian tightening into March is a real headwind and carry is mildly against the short, so the ticket is half the merchant size, short-dated, and cut quickly if the cross extends rather than mean-reverts. Even a half-percent fade covers the official overnight charge on a two-to-three percent adverse path.
